newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat edges sideways on weather, crop bets.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat edges sideways on weather, crop bets.

text.p: Australian wheat futures moved sideways on Monday as betting continued on the weather and the fate of U.S., European and Australian crops.
Only one trade took place, in January 1998, which came back by A$1.00 a tonne to A$187.00 on the trade.
Settlement prices were mixed, falling A$3.00-A$4.00 in near-term contracts, showing some strength in mid-term contracts and a little weakness in more distant contracts.
"There's a bit of indecision here, everyone's looking out across our grain belt and saying it's awfully dry and getting a bit jittery," said Brendan Hillary of ANZ Futures Ltd.
Sellers were still holding back and buyers did not want to pay fair value, creating a standoff, he said.
Hedge interest was creeeping into the market and if rain came in a week's time present prices would be "great", he said.
Some traders were selling futures in Sydney and buying calls in the U.S. as a cover to lock in a price, he said.
All eyes were on the USDA spring wheat planting report, for release after the close of Monday's Chicago trading, he said.
Markets were expected to hover at current levels until the U.S. spring wheat crop was sown, he said.
